tip_title: You Made the Home Inventory. But Did You Write Down What Things Are Actually Worth?
topic: Home Inventory - Valuing Items for Insurance Claims
blurb:
💡 **Insurance Tip: You Made the Home Inventory. But Did You Write Down What Things Are Actually Worth?**

A lot of homeowners have some version of a home inventory — a list, a phone video, a spreadsheet — but most of them stop short of recording the actual value of each item. That gap matters at claim time. Your insurer doesn't just need to know you owned a couch; they need to know what it's worth so they can calculate what you get back. For big-ticket stuff (electronics, jewelry, musical instruments, furniture), keep receipts or note the purchase price and year so there's a real number to work with instead of a guess made under pressure after a loss.

Not sure if your current personal property coverage is in the right ballpark for what you actually own? Your Peachy agent can help you think through it.

📖 [Learn more from NerdWallet](https://www.nerdwallet.com/insurance/homeowners/learn/actual-cash-value-vs-replacement-cost)
summary: Covers the importance of recording item values (not just item names) in a home inventory, so there's a documented number to support a personal property claim rather than an undocumented guess made after a loss.
scoring_notes: Prior tip (2026-04-27) covered HOW to build a home inventory using phone video walkthroughs. This tip takes a substantively different angle: HOW TO VALUE items already on the inventory so they actually support a claim payout. New angle stated explicitly. High homeowner population in both audiences (78% East Cobb). Actionable this week — pull up the inventory and add purchase prices. Evergreen but fresh angle justifies the pick. Source is NerdWallet (trusted list). No carrier names, no dollar figures for premiums.
